title: RTPS: Repplaced new filter with exisiting ones PID Name replaced.
description:
- Coherent sets filters changes to use the exisiting sequenceNumber filter.
- MIG_RTPS_PID_END_COHERENT_SET_SAMPLE_COUNT name replaced with
PID_END_COHERENT_SET_SAMPLE_COUNT name.

notes.body:
How high is the chance, that someone is already using the old name? If so, I would much rather see a change, where the old field is kept and set to hidden (PROTO_ITEM_SET_HIDDEN) and generated (PROTO_ITEM_SET_GENERATED) and in one of the next versions removed. Additionally an expert info should be added informing about the change. Otherwise some filters may break and people may be not entirely sure on what to do.

Especially with RTPS I would caution for a more conservative route to change
I kept the old filters, set the item as hidden, and added the new ones. Also when the filter is used in the filter text bar the description at the bottom warns that it will be deprecated.

  • 43a82ebd...aae500d3 - 8 commits from branch wireshark:master

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4122/diffs?diff_id=241381971&start_sha=43a82ebd8571aa211e25168c4ecd0212405e2da1)
This still poses an issue. Existing filters will fail and people will not be able to fix them properly, because they do not know how.
Only the name changes. The filter value remains the same (rtps.param.id == 0x8024).
I would keep the old fields and element entries, and add the new ones. Also, I would add the expert info explaining the deprecation of the field and moving to the new one

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4122/diffs?diff_id=284532040&start_sha=1e767d335164248b61d7fc2a122b725998d6e26c#02d36cc46f789588510214b5b83b3de5bc4ff57d_15042_15090)
Not being familiar with the protocol I still don't get the "why" of this change.  What is the problem with the 3 existing filters that will be solved by replacing them with the new single filter?
Those fields make more sense with the existing filter "sequenceNumber". They are sequence numbers as well.
